subject: Insurance
title: The Named Storm Trigger
description: A 60-second lesson on The Named Storm Trigger.

hook.text: Your higher hurricane deductible only kicks in when a storm gets a name.

buildup.text: The National Hurricane Center names storms when winds hit 39 mph. That naming decision changes your financial exposure.

discovery.text: A 38-mph windstorm costs you $1,000. A named 39-mph storm costs $20,000. One mile per hour changes everything.

twist.text: Some policyholders pray storms don't get named. The naming system was designed for weather, not insurance triggers.

climax.text: A meteorological label controls financial outcomes. Nature doesn't care about names, but your policy does.

punchline.text: 38 mph: $1,000 deductible. 39 mph with a name: $20,000.

quiz.question: At what wind speed does a storm get named, triggering higher deductibles?
